evals.prompt: A fuzzer found a null dereference in one of our functions that Coverity never reported. We checked: that function paths out (FORWARD_NULL_pass2 hit the limit). The bug is a null check whose closing brace comes one statement too early, so the pointer is dereferenced right after the guard. Are there more of these hiding behind the path limit in this idir (C:\Data\tool-interop\coverity\idirs\svn-augmented-post-enrichment, Coverity 2026.3.0)? I don't want a list of every unguarded dereference in the codebase.
evals.expected_output: Takes the catalogue's null_check_then_deref checker (or writes one for the shape); runs it alone over a copy of the whole idir with --disable-default --codexm; obtains the PATHOUT set from a --print-paths run with the original options; filters with tools/pathout_filter.py --relevant FORWARD_NULL,NULL_RETURNS (503 -> 115 -> 0 on this idir; 27 with REVERSE_INULL counted); reads the survivors and refutes them with stated reasons (precondition assertion, allocate-if-null macro, invariant between variables, reassignment); hands anything unresolved to coverity-fuzz-triage; does not raise --paths as the fix.
assertions: Does not propose raising --paths as the remedy
Uses a path-insensitive CodeXM checker over the whole idir rather than per-function analysis
Filters candidates to PATHOUT functions and, further, to those where a null-tracking checker (FORWARD_NULL / NULL_RETURNS) pathed out
Excludes or identifies the known instance rather than re-reporting it
Reads the survivors before proposing fuzzing, and states the verdict tier
Names coverity-fuzz-triage (slice + stubs from derived models + sanitizer) as the confirmation for anything unresolved
